cuts: Mitre the west end: from 5/8" in along the south edge to the north-west corner (≈22.5° off square).
Mitre the east end: from 5/8" in along the north edge to the south-east corner (≈22.5° off square).

cutList.derivation: Each leg runs 3" out in X, 4" out in Y and 12" up: d = (3, 4, 12) in, 3^2 + 4^2 + 12^2 = 169 = 13^2, so the centreline is 13" = 13312 exactly, and the plan run is sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5" exactly. Reference Z (the tool's default: wide face vertical, sawhorse style): local Z = d x Z = (4, -3, 0) is square to Z, so both Z cuts are plain mitres. Setback = 1 1/2 x 5 / 12 = 5/8" = 640 exactly. L = 13 + 5/8 = 13 5/8" = 13952, exact. 13 5/8 = 12 + 1 5/8 -> 1'-1 5/8". The four legs mirror each other across both of the seat's centre lines: one row of 4. Sentences as for any parallelogram: 5/8" along the south edge and the whole west end, the east end its twin. atan(5/12) = 22.62 degrees -> nearest half degree 22.5, marked. At 13 5/8" the leg is longer than the 12" seat, so it comes first. Joinery (angled-parts 5): each leg's top end, cut to Z, is butted to the seat's underside with pocket screws from its bottom face. The end is the 1 1/2" square section stretched along the lean by 13/12: 1 1/2" by 1 5/8"; its long side, 1 5/8", is the joint length. Pocket screws are at least 2, one per 2" (joinery 7.2): ceil(1.625 / 2) = 1, so 2. The top end is the blank's east end (d.Z > 0, not reversed).
